newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: TAP pilots extend suspension of strike for talks.
newsitem.headline: TAP pilots extend suspension of strike for talks.

text.p: Pilots at struggling Portuguese state airline TAP-Air Portugal on Friday agreed to suspend a selective strike for a further seven days to allow time to reach a deal with the company on working hours, a TAP official said.
"The suspension in the strike has been extended for another seven days to give more time to reach an agreement," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Last Monday, pilots suspended the stoppages for five days until midnight on Friday and have met regularly with senior TAP and government officials over the past week to try to reach agreement.

Twelve flights were cancelled in total last weekend, stranding at least 1,300 people, as pilots refused to operate flights not scheduled at least three days in advance in a protest against the inefficient organisation of their hours.

One government source said that the government and the Civil Aviation Pilots' Union (SPAC), which represents all of TAP's 430 pilots, had reached agreement on several issues, but some matters were still unresolved. He did not elaborate.
The stoppages were due to continue throughout August and the government had warned that they could cause heavy losses for the company during the peak holiday season.
TAP flies international routes and to the Portuguese mid-Atlantic islands of Madeira and the Azores.
The government had said that the pilots' action was risking the survival of the airline, which hopes to return to profit in 1997 after more than two decades of losses.
It says that it is barred by agreements with the European Union from pouring any more funds into the company, which it hopes to privatise, at least partially, before the end of the century.
